title: X Feed Digest
summary: Background-agent UX was the clearest product theme: Gemini Spark framed AI as a 24/7 worker, while Codex posts focused on locked-screen execution and /goal flows that keep jobs moving without babysitting.

The coding-assistant race is shifting from raw model bragging to throughput and orchestration: Antigravity reportedly reset and expanded Gemini quotas again, and Poetiq showed harness design can push a cheaper Flash model much closer to premium behavior.
AI business adoption kept widening beyond pure code tools, with RADAR raising a $170M Series B for in-store physical AI and OpenEvidence shipping voice-first multimodal workflows for physicians.

summary.html: Watch item: GreyNoise flagged fresh SonicWall scanning activity that resembles the lead-up to February's CVE-2026-0400 wave.

items.title: @GeminiApp: Spark Background Agent
items.body: Google positioned Gemini Spark as an always-on agent that can keep working after your phone or laptop goes offline, with human check-ins before major actions. The big signal is product direction: major labs are now selling autonomy and background execution, not just faster chat.

items.title: @xiaohu: Codex on a Locked Mac
items.body: A widely shared walkthrough highlighted Codex's new locked-use flow, which can temporarily unlock a Mac, complete work, and relock it while the display stays protected. That makes agentic coding feel more like remote operations software than a foreground assistant.

items.title: @dotey: /goal Workflow Setup
items.body: This practical post distilled how to turn on and use Codex /goal in the app, including the feature flag step and the new entry point in the UI. It was one of the more useful workflow tips in the batch because it turns a fuzzy feature into something repeatable today.

items.title: @poetiq_ai: Flash Harness Beats Its Weight
items.body: Poetiq said its meta-system improved Gemini 3.5 Flash by more than 10% on LiveCodeBench Pro, enough to match much pricier Deep Think behavior on that coding benchmark. Even if you discount benchmark marketing, the useful takeaway is that harness quality is becoming a real lever, not just a wrapper.

items.title: @0xLogicrw: Antigravity Quotas Reset Again
items.body: A recap of Varun Mohan's announcement said Antigravity again tripled weekly Gemini quotas for paid users, taking effective capacity to about 9x the original baseline and resetting current usage. The market signal is simple: developers now treat model throughput like infrastructure, and they punish fake-feeling limits fast.

items.title: @SpencerHewett: RADAR's $170M Series B
items.body: RADAR announced a $170 million Series B at a valuation above $1 billion, pitching physical AI for the large share of retail commerce that still happens in stores. The financing matters because it shows real capital is flowing into AI systems tied to sensors, inventory, and in-person operations rather than just chat interfaces.

items.title: @dotey: Cloudflare's AI Hiring Swap
items.body: One of the sharper business posts in the feed highlighted Matthew Prince's Wall Street Journal argument about replacing some roles with AI alongside Cloudflare's first major layoff and a similarly sized intern intake. Whether you agree with the framing or not, it is a concrete example of AI changing workforce mix rather than just tool choice.

items.title: @TheSixFiveMedia: Resolution Beats Speed
items.body: This enterprise AI commentary argued that faster responses do not improve service economics if they still escalate, and that teams should optimize for resolution instead. That is a useful operating metric for anyone evaluating AI customer-support vendors or internal copilots.

items.title: @EvidenceOpen: Voice Mode for Clinical AI
items.body: OpenEvidence launched a voice-first mode so physicians can speak, type, or listen while moving through rounds and calls. The interesting part is not just multimodality; it is that clinical AI is being shaped around messy real workflows instead of ideal desk setups.

items.title: @GreyNoiseIO: SonicWall Recon Is Heating Up
items.body: GreyNoise warned that it is seeing SonicWall scanning patterns similar to the activity that preceded February's CVE-2026-0400 wave, with the biggest one-day spike in 90 days on May 12. If you manage edge security gear, this is the most actionable risk signal in the batch.

items.title: @MaxForAI: Codex Built the Deliverable
items.body: A developer shared that after being given an open-source ASR repo and a rough goal, Codex did not just explain the setup but pulled the code, built a front end, deployed it locally, and even fixed a bug. It is anecdotal, but it captures the shift from advice bots toward systems that hand back working artifacts.

items.title: @CARMA_411: Adaptive AI Governance Paper
items.body: CARMA shared a new paper arguing that advanced AI governance needs adaptive institutional structures with explicit failure modes, not just high-level principles. If you follow safety or policy work, it is a more concrete frame than the usual generic governance thread.
